--- a/task_template.md
+++ b/task_template.md
@@ -45,3 +45,7 @@
 2. Solution: compute the answer from the input data and write the modified file to output_path.
 3. Verification (do this before you finish): re-open the file you just wrote, print the cells in answer_position, and check them. Confirm that (a) each cell holds the RIGHT value — filled where the operation produces a value, and left unchanged/blank where the instruction implies no value (do NOT fill a cell with 0 or a placeholder just to avoid a blank), (b) the values have the expected type and format, (c) they were COMPUTED from the input — ask yourself "would this exact code still be correct if the input had different values and a different number of rows?", and (d) they reproduce every concrete example the instruction states, and any example/expected values already present in the file. If any check fails, fix the solution and re-run. You are done only once the file is written AND answer_position reads back correct.
+4. Generalization self-test — DO NOT SKIP; a solution that only reads back correct on THIS file is not enough. The EXACT code you just wrote is automatically re-run on two more input files with this same layout but DIFFERENT values and a DIFFERENT (usually larger) number of rows, and your answer counts ONLY if it is correct on all three. You cannot see those files, so manufacture one now and test against it. AFTER output_path is written from the real input, load the input again into a scratch workbook, MUTATE that scratch copy to look like a plausible hidden variant, and run your SAME solution logic on it (write to a throwaway path, never to output_path). Make the mutation stress the exact things that break over-fit code:
+   - append several extra data rows PAST the current last data row — including at least one new group/segment and a trailing partial group whose closing marker/boundary is missing;
+   - change some values, and if runs/groups/ordering matter, reorder or duplicate a group and insert a blank or a text-where-a-number-was cell.
+   Then print the scratch answer cells and confirm the code (i) runs to completion and reaches its save WITHOUT raising, (ii) still scans to the NEW last row so nothing past the old extent is dropped, and (iii) produces correct per-row / per-group / boundary results for the mutated data — especially the appended rows and the trailing partial group. If any of these is wrong, your code was over-fit to the preview: derive extents and group boundaries from the data (not from preview row counts or the answer range), fix the GENERAL logic, then recompute and re-save output_path from the REAL input. This self-test is diagnostic only — for already-correct code it changes nothing you save; write output_path from the real input FIRST.
 If your code raises an error, the traceback will be returned to you; fix the code and try again.
